Made in Korea (식세기 중 유일)  추가 설치 해도 되고 안 해도 되는: 콘센트가 멀어서 고민하다 싱크대 아래 콘센트에 연결하기로 결정 후 추가금 38,000 결제함(심미적인 부분에 투자하느냐만 선택하면 됨) 멀티탭으로 연결하거나 콘센트가 가까우면 추가 필요 없음. 싱크대 턱에 이미 타공 돼 있어서 배수호스 깔끔하게 연결함 단점: 아직은 없...  설치비는 무료!  카드할인 행사해서 좋은 가격으로 샀구요. 쿠팡은 매일 가격변동이 있고 그때그때 카드할인이나 와우할인 혜택이 생기니 지켜보시다가 가격 좋은 날 구매하시면 돼요. 저는 일요일 밤에 샀는데 월요일에 가격 오르다가 주말 쯤 다시 내리더라고요. 며칠 사이 이벤트가 달라지지만 가격차이가 그리 크진 않았고 하루라도 빨리 설치해서 노동에서 벗어나는 게 돈 버는 길인 듯 해요. 기사님도 친절하셨고 작업은 마무리 사인까지 한 시간 정도 걸렸어요.  6인용 살까말까 고민 중이시면 국낸 생산인 엘지 추천드려요. 저는 12인용보다 훨씬 실용적인 거 같아요. 설거지 스트레스 날려보아요~~~:)

Sentence (English): I think it is much more practical than a 12-person one.
Comments (English): [ Dishwasher Life 25 Years Recommended Items (This is a review of a product I bought with my own money) ] || ---------------- || I started with the LG 6-person dishwasher, then the LG 12-person No. 1, and the Samsung 12-person No. 2. LG was very satisfactory, but I was dissatisfied with the Samsung in terms of cleaning power and durability. So when I moved, I thought I had to go with LG. I couldn't install a 12-person model, so I decided on a countertop 6-person model. I was worried that it would be too small for a family of 3, but it's actually more comfortable, so I highly recommend it :) Advantages 1. Intuitive door opening button. Most models open by bending your wrist, but it's easier on your wrist and more comfortable to open up and down by lightly pressing the button with your finger. 2. Efficient in narrow spaces and not small in any way. It doesn't take up as much space as you'd think, and it has a two-tier tray, so you can put things on top, and you can put tall pots, etc. without removing the upper tray. 3. Stainless steel dish rack. The inner dish rack is made of stainless steel, not plastic silicone coating, so it's luxurious and safe (I liked it the most because the coating sometimes peeled off and rusted). 4. Dual cleaning wings. Two cleaning wings underneath clean evenly. 5. High-temperature water washing, hot air drying, UV sterilization function. It dries in hot air at 80 degrees Celsius, and additionally It also has a sterilizing function, so it's good until it's hot and crispy. It's easy to sterilize and disinfect cutting boards and knives. 6. It's perfect for those who are lazy because you can just drop a spoonful into the concave part of the detergent compartment door. (When using the ** frog, it was cumbersome to cut and the unique smell was hard for a dog person like me, so I settled on the unscented Nelly (powder type), but I recommend Nelly because it leaves almost no stains and has good ingredients. You only need to use a small amount.) 7. After drying the CD with hot air, the CD (Cool Dry) internal ventilation operates. You can stop it with the stop button in the middle and open the door to dry naturally. There is no automatic door opening function, but it seems that there is no problem with the internal drying because of this function. 8. It saves movement, and you can organize dishes right away by opening the sink storage cabinet. 9. It protects your back because you don't have to bend over^^ 10. Made in Korea (the only dishwasher) Additional installation is possible or not: I was worried because the outlet was far away, so I decided to connect it to the outlet under the sink and paid an additional fee of 38,000 (you just have to choose whether to invest in the aesthetic part). If you connect it to a multi-tap or the outlet is close, you don't need to add anything. The sink ledge is already perforated, so you can connect the drain hose neatly. Disadvantages: None yet. Installation fee is free! I bought it at a good price because there was a card discount event. Coupang's prices change every day, and there are card discounts or Wow discount benefits at that time, so you can watch and buy it on a good day. I bought it on Sunday night, and the price went up on Monday and then went down again around the weekend. The event changes in a few days, but the price difference is not that big, and it seems that the way to make money is to install it as soon as possible and get rid of labor. The technician was kind and the work took about an hour to complete. If you are thinking about buying a 6-person one, I recommend LG, which is a domestically produced product. I think it is much more practical than a 12-person one. Let's blow away the stress of washing dishes~~~:)

Made in Korea (식세기 중 유일)  추가 설치 해도 되고 안 해도 되는: 콘센트가 멀어서 고민하다 싱크대 아래 콘센트에 연결하기로 결정 후 추가금 38,000 결제함(심미적인 부분에 투자하느냐만 선택하면 됨) 멀티탭으로 연결하거나 콘센트가 가까우면 추가 필요 없음. 싱크대 턱에 이미 타공 돼 있어서 배수호스 깔끔하게 연결함 단점: 아직은 없...  설치비는 무료!  카드할인 행사해서 좋은 가격으로 샀구요. 쿠팡은 매일 가격변동이 있고 그때그때 카드할인이나 와우할인 혜택이 생기니 지켜보시다가 가격 좋은 날 구매하시면 돼요. 저는 일요일 밤에 샀는데 월요일에 가격 오르다가 주말 쯤 다시 내리더라고요. 며칠 사이 이벤트가 달라지지만 가격차이가 그리 크진 않았고 하루라도 빨리 설치해서 노동에서 벗어나는 게 돈 버는 길인 듯 해요. 기사님도 친절하셨고 작업은 마무리 사인까지 한 시간 정도 걸렸어요.  6인용 살까말까 고민 중이시면 국낸 생산인 엘지 추천드려요. 저는 12인용보다 훨씬 실용적인 거 같아요. 설거지 스트레스 날려보아요~~~:)

Sentence (English): There's water on the cup that I turned over and there's moisture left on the silicone packing of the lunch box lid.
Comments (English): [ Price drop just two days after purchase? ] || ---------------- || If you bought it on Sunday and installed it on Tuesday morning and the price went down by 40,000 won in the meantime, would you feel good? Or not? It doesn't dry properly after washing the dishes. There's water on the cup that I turned over and there's moisture left on the silicone packing of the lunch box lid. Even though I left it wide open for 30-40 minutes, it was like that (there was still moisture left the next morning). You have to take the cup out and shake off the water. Don't be afraid of electricity and add the 'strong drying' stage to see about 80% drying effect and there are also fewer water stains. Standard course, basic 4 rinses (1:08) + strong drying = 1 hour 26 minutes, and if you add a rinse when there are a lot of dishes, it takes about 1 hour 37 minutes in total. (Since I run it after washing the dishes first, the standard course and basic rinse are enough). At first, I ran it on the strong drying cycle for a while, but since people are creatures of adaptation, I just roughly ran the standard cycle and after washing the dishes, I took out the Lock & Lock lid and cup, shook off the water, and put them back to dry. I had this problem when I used a large built-in before, so I considered using a dishwasher, but the dish dryer broke down, so I ended up getting a dishwasher. It seems that a dryer is the best for fluffy drying + sterilization! The dishwashing time was saved by half compared to usual, but it seems like a different type of annoying aftercare. I felt uncomfortable about having to leave the door open for drying, as I was worried that dust or flies might get in. I have no complaints about the installer. He was neat, kind, and installed it quickly. This is an honest review from a consumer who spent 40,000 won in two days and was very upset. -Additional review 1- As a detergent tip, even if it says 6 tablets, I don't think you need to put in every single tablet. I cut it into 5:5 parts with scissors and put it in a container and use it, and it's clean. I used up one. It feels a bit slippery. I wonder if I should add a rinse. It is definitely too small to wash large cooking utensils like frying pans and pots together with the dishes (for a family of two). They just wash their dishes by hand. Anyway, although the drying function is disappointing, it is good to have a dishwasher. Don't suffer from plantar fasciitis and varicose veins later, and if you are hooked, buy it. -Additional review 2- If you are disappointed that there is no 'rinse only' function, you can use 'quick course' + 'add rinse' to finish washing the dishes cleanly in about 34 minutes (about 10 minutes of washing process - dehydration - 3 rinses = total 4 rinses). In fact, this is how I wash the dishes these days. Since I am a novice, I just invest 5 more minutes, put dishwashing detergent on a sponge, wipe it, and rinse it. It seems cleaner when I do it by hand, and I wonder if I bought it and made a fuss. I want to, but the dishwashing time and effort have been reduced incomparably compared to when there was no dishwasher. The condition of the dishes after washing is the best, boasting a shiny and glossy finish^^. (I don't use tablets, so I don't have to spend money on that) Electricity, water, and sewage bills, and hot water bills have also been reduced by tens of thousands of won compared to before the dishwasher (when I used a dish dryer), so I think this is enough. Thank you for reading the long review. Have a nice day^^

Sentence (English): You have to take the cup out and shake off the water.
Comments (English): [ Price drop just two days after purchase? ] || ---------------- || If you bought it on Sunday and installed it on Tuesday morning and the price went down by 40,000 won in the meantime, would you feel good? Or not? It doesn't dry properly after washing the dishes. There's water on the cup that I turned over and there's moisture left on the silicone packing of the lunch box lid. Even though I left it wide open for 30-40 minutes, it was like that (there was still moisture left the next morning). You have to take the cup out and shake off the water. Don't be afraid of electricity and add the 'strong drying' stage to see about 80% drying effect and there are also fewer water stains. Standard course, basic 4 rinses (1:08) + strong drying = 1 hour 26 minutes, and if you add a rinse when there are a lot of dishes, it takes about 1 hour 37 minutes in total. (Since I run it after washing the dishes first, the standard course and basic rinse are enough). At first, I ran it on the strong drying cycle for a while, but since people are creatures of adaptation, I just roughly ran the standard cycle and after washing the dishes, I took out the Lock & Lock lid and cup, shook off the water, and put them back to dry. I had this problem when I used a large built-in before, so I considered using a dishwasher, but the dish dryer broke down, so I ended up getting a dishwasher. It seems that a dryer is the best for fluffy drying + sterilization! The dishwashing time was saved by half compared to usual, but it seems like a different type of annoying aftercare. I felt uncomfortable about having to leave the door open for drying, as I was worried that dust or flies might get in. I have no complaints about the installer. He was neat, kind, and installed it quickly. This is an honest review from a consumer who spent 40,000 won in two days and was very upset. -Additional review 1- As a detergent tip, even if it says 6 tablets, I don't think you need to put in every single tablet. I cut it into 5:5 parts with scissors and put it in a container and use it, and it's clean. I used up one. It feels a bit slippery. I wonder if I should add a rinse. It is definitely too small to wash large cooking utensils like frying pans and pots together with the dishes (for a family of two). They just wash their dishes by hand. Anyway, although the drying function is disappointing, it is good to have a dishwasher. Don't suffer from plantar fasciitis and varicose veins later, and if you are hooked, buy it. -Additional review 2- If you are disappointed that there is no 'rinse only' function, you can use 'quick course' + 'add rinse' to finish washing the dishes cleanly in about 34 minutes (about 10 minutes of washing process - dehydration - 3 rinses = total 4 rinses). In fact, this is how I wash the dishes these days. Since I am a novice, I just invest 5 more minutes, put dishwashing detergent on a sponge, wipe it, and rinse it. It seems cleaner when I do it by hand, and I wonder if I bought it and made a fuss. I want to, but the dishwashing time and effort have been reduced incomparably compared to when there was no dishwasher. The condition of the dishes after washing is the best, boasting a shiny and glossy finish^^. (I don't use tablets, so I don't have to spend money on that) Electricity, water, and sewage bills, and hot water bills have also been reduced by tens of thousands of won compared to before the dishwasher (when I used a dish dryer), so I think this is enough. Thank you for reading the long review. Have a nice day^^

Sentence (English): Standard course, basic 4 rinses (1:08) + strong drying = 1 hour 26 minutes, and if you add a rinse when there are a lot of dishes, it takes about 1 hour 37 minutes in total. (
Comments (English): [ Price drop just two days after purchase? ] || ---------------- || If you bought it on Sunday and installed it on Tuesday morning and the price went down by 40,000 won in the meantime, would you feel good? Or not? It doesn't dry properly after washing the dishes. There's water on the cup that I turned over and there's moisture left on the silicone packing of the lunch box lid. Even though I left it wide open for 30-40 minutes, it was like that (there was still moisture left the next morning). You have to take the cup out and shake off the water. Don't be afraid of electricity and add the 'strong drying' stage to see about 80% drying effect and there are also fewer water stains. Standard course, basic 4 rinses (1:08) + strong drying = 1 hour 26 minutes, and if you add a rinse when there are a lot of dishes, it takes about 1 hour 37 minutes in total. (Since I run it after washing the dishes first, the standard course and basic rinse are enough). At first, I ran it on the strong drying cycle for a while, but since people are creatures of adaptation, I just roughly ran the standard cycle and after washing the dishes, I took out the Lock & Lock lid and cup, shook off the water, and put them back to dry. I had this problem when I used a large built-in before, so I considered using a dishwasher, but the dish dryer broke down, so I ended up getting a dishwasher. It seems that a dryer is the best for fluffy drying + sterilization! The dishwashing time was saved by half compared to usual, but it seems like a different type of annoying aftercare. I felt uncomfortable about having to leave the door open for drying, as I was worried that dust or flies might get in. I have no complaints about the installer. He was neat, kind, and installed it quickly. This is an honest review from a consumer who spent 40,000 won in two days and was very upset. -Additional review 1- As a detergent tip, even if it says 6 tablets, I don't think you need to put in every single tablet. I cut it into 5:5 parts with scissors and put it in a container and use it, and it's clean. I used up one. It feels a bit slippery. I wonder if I should add a rinse. It is definitely too small to wash large cooking utensils like frying pans and pots together with the dishes (for a family of two). They just wash their dishes by hand. Anyway, although the drying function is disappointing, it is good to have a dishwasher. Don't suffer from plantar fasciitis and varicose veins later, and if you are hooked, buy it. -Additional review 2- If you are disappointed that there is no 'rinse only' function, you can use 'quick course' + 'add rinse' to finish washing the dishes cleanly in about 34 minutes (about 10 minutes of washing process - dehydration - 3 rinses = total 4 rinses). In fact, this is how I wash the dishes these days. Since I am a novice, I just invest 5 more minutes, put dishwashing detergent on a sponge, wipe it, and rinse it. It seems cleaner when I do it by hand, and I wonder if I bought it and made a fuss. I want to, but the dishwashing time and effort have been reduced incomparably compared to when there was no dishwasher. The condition of the dishes after washing is the best, boasting a shiny and glossy finish^^. (I don't use tablets, so I don't have to spend money on that) Electricity, water, and sewage bills, and hot water bills have also been reduced by tens of thousands of won compared to before the dishwasher (when I used a dish dryer), so I think this is enough. Thank you for reading the long review. Have a nice day^^

Comments (English): [ Price drop just two days after purchase? ] || ---------------- || If you bought it on Sunday and installed it on Tuesday morning and the price went down by 40,000 won in the meantime, would you feel good? Or not? It doesn't dry properly after washing the dishes. There's water on the cup that I turned over and there's moisture left on the silicone packing of the lunch box lid. Even though I left it wide open for 30-40 minutes, it was like that (there was still moisture left the next morning). You have to take the cup out and shake off the water. Don't be afraid of electricity and add the 'strong drying' stage to see about 80% drying effect and there are also fewer water stains. Standard course, basic 4 rinses (1:08) + strong drying = 1 hour 26 minutes, and if you add a rinse when there are a lot of dishes, it takes about 1 hour 37 minutes in total. (Since I run it after washing the dishes first, the standard course and basic rinse are enough). At first, I ran it on the strong drying cycle for a while, but since people are creatures of adaptation, I just roughly ran the standard cycle and after washing the dishes, I took out the Lock & Lock lid and cup, shook off the water, and put them back to dry. I had this problem when I used a large built-in before, so I considered using a dishwasher, but the dish dryer broke down, so I ended up getting a dishwasher. It seems that a dryer is the best for fluffy drying + sterilization! The dishwashing time was saved by half compared to usual, but it seems like a different type of annoying aftercare. I felt uncomfortable about having to leave the door open for drying, as I was worried that dust or flies might get in. I have no complaints about the installer. He was neat, kind, and installed it quickly. This is an honest review from a consumer who spent 40,000 won in two days and was very upset. -Additional review 1- As a detergent tip, even if it says 6 tablets, I don't think you need to put in every single tablet. I cut it into 5:5 parts with scissors and put it in a container and use it, and it's clean. I used up one. It feels a bit slippery. I wonder if I should add a rinse. It is definitely too small to wash large cooking utensils like frying pans and pots together with the dishes (for a family of two). They just wash their dishes by hand. Anyway, although the drying function is disappointing, it is good to have a dishwasher. Don't suffer from plantar fasciitis and varicose veins later, and if you are hooked, buy it. -Additional review 2- If you are disappointed that there is no 'rinse only' function, you can use 'quick course' + 'add rinse' to finish washing the dishes cleanly in about 34 minutes (about 10 minutes of washing process - dehydration - 3 rinses = total 4 rinses). In fact, this is how I wash the dishes these days. Since I am a novice, I just invest 5 more minutes, put dishwashing detergent on a sponge, wipe it, and rinse it. It seems cleaner when I do it by hand, and I wonder if I bought it and made a fuss. I want to, but the dishwashing time and effort have been reduced incomparably compared to when there was no dishwasher. The condition of the dishes after washing is the best, boasting a shiny and glossy finish^^. (I don't use tablets, so I don't have to spend money on that) Electricity, water, and sewage bills, and hot water bills have also been reduced by tens of thousands of won compared to before the dishwasher (when I used a dish dryer), so I think this is enough. Thank you for reading the long review. Have a nice day^^

Sentence (English): I had this problem when I used a large built-in before, so I considered using a dishwasher, but the dish dryer broke down, so I ended up getting a dishwasher.
Comments (English): [ Price drop just two days after purchase? ] || ---------------- || If you bought it on Sunday and installed it on Tuesday morning and the price went down by 40,000 won in the meantime, would you feel good? Or not? It doesn't dry properly after washing the dishes. There's water on the cup that I turned over and there's moisture left on the silicone packing of the lunch box lid. Even though I left it wide open for 30-40 minutes, it was like that (there was still moisture left the next morning). You have to take the cup out and shake off the water. Don't be afraid of electricity and add the 'strong drying' stage to see about 80% drying effect and there are also fewer water stains. Standard course, basic 4 rinses (1:08) + strong drying = 1 hour 26 minutes, and if you add a rinse when there are a lot of dishes, it takes about 1 hour 37 minutes in total. (Since I run it after washing the dishes first, the standard course and basic rinse are enough). At first, I ran it on the strong drying cycle for a while, but since people are creatures of adaptation, I just roughly ran the standard cycle and after washing the dishes, I took out the Lock & Lock lid and cup, shook off the water, and put them back to dry. I had this problem when I used a large built-in before, so I considered using a dishwasher, but the dish dryer broke down, so I ended up getting a dishwasher. It seems that a dryer is the best for fluffy drying + sterilization! The dishwashing time was saved by half compared to usual, but it seems like a different type of annoying aftercare. I felt uncomfortable about having to leave the door open for drying, as I was worried that dust or flies might get in. I have no complaints about the installer. He was neat, kind, and installed it quickly. This is an honest review from a consumer who spent 40,000 won in two days and was very upset. -Additional review 1- As a detergent tip, even if it says 6 tablets, I don't think you need to put in every single tablet. I cut it into 5:5 parts with scissors and put it in a container and use it, and it's clean. I used up one. It feels a bit slippery. I wonder if I should add a rinse. It is definitely too small to wash large cooking utensils like frying pans and pots together with the dishes (for a family of two). They just wash their dishes by hand. Anyway, although the drying function is disappointing, it is good to have a dishwasher. Don't suffer from plantar fasciitis and varicose veins later, and if you are hooked, buy it. -Additional review 2- If you are disappointed that there is no 'rinse only' function, you can use 'quick course' + 'add rinse' to finish washing the dishes cleanly in about 34 minutes (about 10 minutes of washing process - dehydration - 3 rinses = total 4 rinses). In fact, this is how I wash the dishes these days. Since I am a novice, I just invest 5 more minutes, put dishwashing detergent on a sponge, wipe it, and rinse it. It seems cleaner when I do it by hand, and I wonder if I bought it and made a fuss. I want to, but the dishwashing time and effort have been reduced incomparably compared to when there was no dishwasher. The condition of the dishes after washing is the best, boasting a shiny and glossy finish^^. (I don't use tablets, so I don't have to spend money on that) Electricity, water, and sewage bills, and hot water bills have also been reduced by tens of thousands of won compared to before the dishwasher (when I used a dish dryer), so I think this is enough. Thank you for reading the long review. Have a nice day^^

Sentence (English): The dishwashing time was saved by half compared to usual, but it seems like a different type of annoying aftercare.
Comments (English): [ Price drop just two days after purchase? ] || ---------------- || If you bought it on Sunday and installed it on Tuesday morning and the price went down by 40,000 won in the meantime, would you feel good? Or not? It doesn't dry properly after washing the dishes. There's water on the cup that I turned over and there's moisture left on the silicone packing of the lunch box lid. Even though I left it wide open for 30-40 minutes, it was like that (there was still moisture left the next morning). You have to take the cup out and shake off the water. Don't be afraid of electricity and add the 'strong drying' stage to see about 80% drying effect and there are also fewer water stains. Standard course, basic 4 rinses (1:08) + strong drying = 1 hour 26 minutes, and if you add a rinse when there are a lot of dishes, it takes about 1 hour 37 minutes in total. (Since I run it after washing the dishes first, the standard course and basic rinse are enough). At first, I ran it on the strong drying cycle for a while, but since people are creatures of adaptation, I just roughly ran the standard cycle and after washing the dishes, I took out the Lock & Lock lid and cup, shook off the water, and put them back to dry. I had this problem when I used a large built-in before, so I considered using a dishwasher, but the dish dryer broke down, so I ended up getting a dishwasher. It seems that a dryer is the best for fluffy drying + sterilization! The dishwashing time was saved by half compared to usual, but it seems like a different type of annoying aftercare. I felt uncomfortable about having to leave the door open for drying, as I was worried that dust or flies might get in. I have no complaints about the installer. He was neat, kind, and installed it quickly. This is an honest review from a consumer who spent 40,000 won in two days and was very upset. -Additional review 1- As a detergent tip, even if it says 6 tablets, I don't think you need to put in every single tablet. I cut it into 5:5 parts with scissors and put it in a container and use it, and it's clean. I used up one. It feels a bit slippery. I wonder if I should add a rinse. It is definitely too small to wash large cooking utensils like frying pans and pots together with the dishes (for a family of two). They just wash their dishes by hand. Anyway, although the drying function is disappointing, it is good to have a dishwasher. Don't suffer from plantar fasciitis and varicose veins later, and if you are hooked, buy it. -Additional review 2- If you are disappointed that there is no 'rinse only' function, you can use 'quick course' + 'add rinse' to finish washing the dishes cleanly in about 34 minutes (about 10 minutes of washing process - dehydration - 3 rinses = total 4 rinses). In fact, this is how I wash the dishes these days. Since I am a novice, I just invest 5 more minutes, put dishwashing detergent on a sponge, wipe it, and rinse it. It seems cleaner when I do it by hand, and I wonder if I bought it and made a fuss. I want to, but the dishwashing time and effort have been reduced incomparably compared to when there was no dishwasher. The condition of the dishes after washing is the best, boasting a shiny and glossy finish^^. (I don't use tablets, so I don't have to spend money on that) Electricity, water, and sewage bills, and hot water bills have also been reduced by tens of thousands of won compared to before the dishwasher (when I used a dish dryer), so I think this is enough. Thank you for reading the long review. Have a nice day^^

Sentence (English): I felt uncomfortable about having to leave the door open for drying, as I was worried that dust or flies might get in.
Comments (English): [ Price drop just two days after purchase? ] || ---------------- || If you bought it on Sunday and installed it on Tuesday morning and the price went down by 40,000 won in the meantime, would you feel good? Or not? It doesn't dry properly after washing the dishes. There's water on the cup that I turned over and there's moisture left on the silicone packing of the lunch box lid. Even though I left it wide open for 30-40 minutes, it was like that (there was still moisture left the next morning). You have to take the cup out and shake off the water. Don't be afraid of electricity and add the 'strong drying' stage to see about 80% drying effect and there are also fewer water stains. Standard course, basic 4 rinses (1:08) + strong drying = 1 hour 26 minutes, and if you add a rinse when there are a lot of dishes, it takes about 1 hour 37 minutes in total. (Since I run it after washing the dishes first, the standard course and basic rinse are enough). At first, I ran it on the strong drying cycle for a while, but since people are creatures of adaptation, I just roughly ran the standard cycle and after washing the dishes, I took out the Lock & Lock lid and cup, shook off the water, and put them back to dry. I had this problem when I used a large built-in before, so I considered using a dishwasher, but the dish dryer broke down, so I ended up getting a dishwasher. It seems that a dryer is the best for fluffy drying + sterilization! The dishwashing time was saved by half compared to usual, but it seems like a different type of annoying aftercare. I felt uncomfortable about having to leave the door open for drying, as I was worried that dust or flies might get in. I have no complaints about the installer. He was neat, kind, and installed it quickly. This is an honest review from a consumer who spent 40,000 won in two days and was very upset. -Additional review 1- As a detergent tip, even if it says 6 tablets, I don't think you need to put in every single tablet. I cut it into 5:5 parts with scissors and put it in a container and use it, and it's clean. I used up one. It feels a bit slippery. I wonder if I should add a rinse. It is definitely too small to wash large cooking utensils like frying pans and pots together with the dishes (for a family of two). They just wash their dishes by hand. Anyway, although the drying function is disappointing, it is good to have a dishwasher. Don't suffer from plantar fasciitis and varicose veins later, and if you are hooked, buy it. -Additional review 2- If you are disappointed that there is no 'rinse only' function, you can use 'quick course' + 'add rinse' to finish washing the dishes cleanly in about 34 minutes (about 10 minutes of washing process - dehydration - 3 rinses = total 4 rinses). In fact, this is how I wash the dishes these days. Since I am a novice, I just invest 5 more minutes, put dishwashing detergent on a sponge, wipe it, and rinse it. It seems cleaner when I do it by hand, and I wonder if I bought it and made a fuss. I want to, but the dishwashing time and effort have been reduced incomparably compared to when there was no dishwasher. The condition of the dishes after washing is the best, boasting a shiny and glossy finish^^. (I don't use tablets, so I don't have to spend money on that) Electricity, water, and sewage bills, and hot water bills have also been reduced by tens of thousands of won compared to before the dishwasher (when I used a dish dryer), so I think this is enough. Thank you for reading the long review. Have a nice day^^

Sentence (English): He was neat, kind, and installed it quickly.
Comments (English): [ Price drop just two days after purchase? ] || ---------------- || If you bought it on Sunday and installed it on Tuesday morning and the price went down by 40,000 won in the meantime, would you feel good? Or not? It doesn't dry properly after washing the dishes. There's water on the cup that I turned over and there's moisture left on the silicone packing of the lunch box lid. Even though I left it wide open for 30-40 minutes, it was like that (there was still moisture left the next morning). You have to take the cup out and shake off the water. Don't be afraid of electricity and add the 'strong drying' stage to see about 80% drying effect and there are also fewer water stains. Standard course, basic 4 rinses (1:08) + strong drying = 1 hour 26 minutes, and if you add a rinse when there are a lot of dishes, it takes about 1 hour 37 minutes in total. (Since I run it after washing the dishes first, the standard course and basic rinse are enough). At first, I ran it on the strong drying cycle for a while, but since people are creatures of adaptation, I just roughly ran the standard cycle and after washing the dishes, I took out the Lock & Lock lid and cup, shook off the water, and put them back to dry. I had this problem when I used a large built-in before, so I considered using a dishwasher, but the dish dryer broke down, so I ended up getting a dishwasher. It seems that a dryer is the best for fluffy drying + sterilization! The dishwashing time was saved by half compared to usual, but it seems like a different type of annoying aftercare. I felt uncomfortable about having to leave the door open for drying, as I was worried that dust or flies might get in. I have no complaints about the installer. He was neat, kind, and installed it quickly. This is an honest review from a consumer who spent 40,000 won in two days and was very upset. -Additional review 1- As a detergent tip, even if it says 6 tablets, I don't think you need to put in every single tablet. I cut it into 5:5 parts with scissors and put it in a container and use it, and it's clean. I used up one. It feels a bit slippery. I wonder if I should add a rinse. It is definitely too small to wash large cooking utensils like frying pans and pots together with the dishes (for a family of two). They just wash their dishes by hand. Anyway, although the drying function is disappointing, it is good to have a dishwasher. Don't suffer from plantar fasciitis and varicose veins later, and if you are hooked, buy it. -Additional review 2- If you are disappointed that there is no 'rinse only' function, you can use 'quick course' + 'add rinse' to finish washing the dishes cleanly in about 34 minutes (about 10 minutes of washing process - dehydration - 3 rinses = total 4 rinses). In fact, this is how I wash the dishes these days. Since I am a novice, I just invest 5 more minutes, put dishwashing detergent on a sponge, wipe it, and rinse it. It seems cleaner when I do it by hand, and I wonder if I bought it and made a fuss. I want to, but the dishwashing time and effort have been reduced incomparably compared to when there was no dishwasher. The condition of the dishes after washing is the best, boasting a shiny and glossy finish^^. (I don't use tablets, so I don't have to spend money on that) Electricity, water, and sewage bills, and hot water bills have also been reduced by tens of thousands of won compared to before the dishwasher (when I used a dish dryer), so I think this is enough. Thank you for reading the long review. Have a nice day^^

Comments (English): [ Price drop just two days after purchase? ] || ---------------- || If you bought it on Sunday and installed it on Tuesday morning and the price went down by 40,000 won in the meantime, would you feel good? Or not? It doesn't dry properly after washing the dishes. There's water on the cup that I turned over and there's moisture left on the silicone packing of the lunch box lid. Even though I left it wide open for 30-40 minutes, it was like that (there was still moisture left the next morning). You have to take the cup out and shake off the water. Don't be afraid of electricity and add the 'strong drying' stage to see about 80% drying effect and there are also fewer water stains. Standard course, basic 4 rinses (1:08) + strong drying = 1 hour 26 minutes, and if you add a rinse when there are a lot of dishes, it takes about 1 hour 37 minutes in total. (Since I run it after washing the dishes first, the standard course and basic rinse are enough). At first, I ran it on the strong drying cycle for a while, but since people are creatures of adaptation, I just roughly ran the standard cycle and after washing the dishes, I took out the Lock & Lock lid and cup, shook off the water, and put them back to dry. I had this problem when I used a large built-in before, so I considered using a dishwasher, but the dish dryer broke down, so I ended up getting a dishwasher. It seems that a dryer is the best for fluffy drying + sterilization! The dishwashing time was saved by half compared to usual, but it seems like a different type of annoying aftercare. I felt uncomfortable about having to leave the door open for drying, as I was worried that dust or flies might get in. I have no complaints about the installer. He was neat, kind, and installed it quickly. This is an honest review from a consumer who spent 40,000 won in two days and was very upset. -Additional review 1- As a detergent tip, even if it says 6 tablets, I don't think you need to put in every single tablet. I cut it into 5:5 parts with scissors and put it in a container and use it, and it's clean. I used up one. It feels a bit slippery. I wonder if I should add a rinse. It is definitely too small to wash large cooking utensils like frying pans and pots together with the dishes (for a family of two). They just wash their dishes by hand. Anyway, although the drying function is disappointing, it is good to have a dishwasher. Don't suffer from plantar fasciitis and varicose veins later, and if you are hooked, buy it. -Additional review 2- If you are disappointed that there is no 'rinse only' function, you can use 'quick course' + 'add rinse' to finish washing the dishes cleanly in about 34 minutes (about 10 minutes of washing process - dehydration - 3 rinses = total 4 rinses). In fact, this is how I wash the dishes these days. Since I am a novice, I just invest 5 more minutes, put dishwashing detergent on a sponge, wipe it, and rinse it. It seems cleaner when I do it by hand, and I wonder if I bought it and made a fuss. I want to, but the dishwashing time and effort have been reduced incomparably compared to when there was no dishwasher. The condition of the dishes after washing is the best, boasting a shiny and glossy finish^^. (I don't use tablets, so I don't have to spend money on that) Electricity, water, and sewage bills, and hot water bills have also been reduced by tens of thousands of won compared to before the dishwasher (when I used a dish dryer), so I think this is enough. Thank you for reading the long review. Have a nice day^^

Sentence (English): I used up one.
Comments (English): [ Price drop just two days after purchase? ] || ---------------- || If you bought it on Sunday and installed it on Tuesday morning and the price went down by 40,000 won in the meantime, would you feel good? Or not? It doesn't dry properly after washing the dishes. There's water on the cup that I turned over and there's moisture left on the silicone packing of the lunch box lid. Even though I left it wide open for 30-40 minutes, it was like that (there was still moisture left the next morning). You have to take the cup out and shake off the water. Don't be afraid of electricity and add the 'strong drying' stage to see about 80% drying effect and there are also fewer water stains. Standard course, basic 4 rinses (1:08) + strong drying = 1 hour 26 minutes, and if you add a rinse when there are a lot of dishes, it takes about 1 hour 37 minutes in total. (Since I run it after washing the dishes first, the standard course and basic rinse are enough). At first, I ran it on the strong drying cycle for a while, but since people are creatures of adaptation, I just roughly ran the standard cycle and after washing the dishes, I took out the Lock & Lock lid and cup, shook off the water, and put them back to dry. I had this problem when I used a large built-in before, so I considered using a dishwasher, but the dish dryer broke down, so I ended up getting a dishwasher. It seems that a dryer is the best for fluffy drying + sterilization! The dishwashing time was saved by half compared to usual, but it seems like a different type of annoying aftercare. I felt uncomfortable about having to leave the door open for drying, as I was worried that dust or flies might get in. I have no complaints about the installer. He was neat, kind, and installed it quickly. This is an honest review from a consumer who spent 40,000 won in two days and was very upset. -Additional review 1- As a detergent tip, even if it says 6 tablets, I don't think you need to put in every single tablet. I cut it into 5:5 parts with scissors and put it in a container and use it, and it's clean. I used up one. It feels a bit slippery. I wonder if I should add a rinse. It is definitely too small to wash large cooking utensils like frying pans and pots together with the dishes (for a family of two). They just wash their dishes by hand. Anyway, although the drying function is disappointing, it is good to have a dishwasher. Don't suffer from plantar fasciitis and varicose veins later, and if you are hooked, buy it. -Additional review 2- If you are disappointed that there is no 'rinse only' function, you can use 'quick course' + 'add rinse' to finish washing the dishes cleanly in about 34 minutes (about 10 minutes of washing process - dehydration - 3 rinses = total 4 rinses). In fact, this is how I wash the dishes these days. Since I am a novice, I just invest 5 more minutes, put dishwashing detergent on a sponge, wipe it, and rinse it. It seems cleaner when I do it by hand, and I wonder if I bought it and made a fuss. I want to, but the dishwashing time and effort have been reduced incomparably compared to when there was no dishwasher. The condition of the dishes after washing is the best, boasting a shiny and glossy finish^^. (I don't use tablets, so I don't have to spend money on that) Electricity, water, and sewage bills, and hot water bills have also been reduced by tens of thousands of won compared to before the dishwasher (when I used a dish dryer), so I think this is enough. Thank you for reading the long review. Have a nice day^^

Sentence (English): I wonder if I should add a rinse.
Comments (English): [ Price drop just two days after purchase? ] || ---------------- || If you bought it on Sunday and installed it on Tuesday morning and the price went down by 40,000 won in the meantime, would you feel good? Or not? It doesn't dry properly after washing the dishes. There's water on the cup that I turned over and there's moisture left on the silicone packing of the lunch box lid. Even though I left it wide open for 30-40 minutes, it was like that (there was still moisture left the next morning). You have to take the cup out and shake off the water. Don't be afraid of electricity and add the 'strong drying' stage to see about 80% drying effect and there are also fewer water stains. Standard course, basic 4 rinses (1:08) + strong drying = 1 hour 26 minutes, and if you add a rinse when there are a lot of dishes, it takes about 1 hour 37 minutes in total. (Since I run it after washing the dishes first, the standard course and basic rinse are enough). At first, I ran it on the strong drying cycle for a while, but since people are creatures of adaptation, I just roughly ran the standard cycle and after washing the dishes, I took out the Lock & Lock lid and cup, shook off the water, and put them back to dry. I had this problem when I used a large built-in before, so I considered using a dishwasher, but the dish dryer broke down, so I ended up getting a dishwasher. It seems that a dryer is the best for fluffy drying + sterilization! The dishwashing time was saved by half compared to usual, but it seems like a different type of annoying aftercare. I felt uncomfortable about having to leave the door open for drying, as I was worried that dust or flies might get in. I have no complaints about the installer. He was neat, kind, and installed it quickly. This is an honest review from a consumer who spent 40,000 won in two days and was very upset. -Additional review 1- As a detergent tip, even if it says 6 tablets, I don't think you need to put in every single tablet. I cut it into 5:5 parts with scissors and put it in a container and use it, and it's clean. I used up one. It feels a bit slippery. I wonder if I should add a rinse. It is definitely too small to wash large cooking utensils like frying pans and pots together with the dishes (for a family of two). They just wash their dishes by hand. Anyway, although the drying function is disappointing, it is good to have a dishwasher. Don't suffer from plantar fasciitis and varicose veins later, and if you are hooked, buy it. -Additional review 2- If you are disappointed that there is no 'rinse only' function, you can use 'quick course' + 'add rinse' to finish washing the dishes cleanly in about 34 minutes (about 10 minutes of washing process - dehydration - 3 rinses = total 4 rinses). In fact, this is how I wash the dishes these days. Since I am a novice, I just invest 5 more minutes, put dishwashing detergent on a sponge, wipe it, and rinse it. It seems cleaner when I do it by hand, and I wonder if I bought it and made a fuss. I want to, but the dishwashing time and effort have been reduced incomparably compared to when there was no dishwasher. The condition of the dishes after washing is the best, boasting a shiny and glossy finish^^. (I don't use tablets, so I don't have to spend money on that) Electricity, water, and sewage bills, and hot water bills have also been reduced by tens of thousands of won compared to before the dishwasher (when I used a dish dryer), so I think this is enough. Thank you for reading the long review. Have a nice day^^

Sentence (English): They just wash their dishes by hand.
Comments (English): [ Price drop just two days after purchase? ] || ---------------- || If you bought it on Sunday and installed it on Tuesday morning and the price went down by 40,000 won in the meantime, would you feel good? Or not? It doesn't dry properly after washing the dishes. There's water on the cup that I turned over and there's moisture left on the silicone packing of the lunch box lid. Even though I left it wide open for 30-40 minutes, it was like that (there was still moisture left the next morning). You have to take the cup out and shake off the water. Don't be afraid of electricity and add the 'strong drying' stage to see about 80% drying effect and there are also fewer water stains. Standard course, basic 4 rinses (1:08) + strong drying = 1 hour 26 minutes, and if you add a rinse when there are a lot of dishes, it takes about 1 hour 37 minutes in total. (Since I run it after washing the dishes first, the standard course and basic rinse are enough). At first, I ran it on the strong drying cycle for a while, but since people are creatures of adaptation, I just roughly ran the standard cycle and after washing the dishes, I took out the Lock & Lock lid and cup, shook off the water, and put them back to dry. I had this problem when I used a large built-in before, so I considered using a dishwasher, but the dish dryer broke down, so I ended up getting a dishwasher. It seems that a dryer is the best for fluffy drying + sterilization! The dishwashing time was saved by half compared to usual, but it seems like a different type of annoying aftercare. I felt uncomfortable about having to leave the door open for drying, as I was worried that dust or flies might get in. I have no complaints about the installer. He was neat, kind, and installed it quickly. This is an honest review from a consumer who spent 40,000 won in two days and was very upset. -Additional review 1- As a detergent tip, even if it says 6 tablets, I don't think you need to put in every single tablet. I cut it into 5:5 parts with scissors and put it in a container and use it, and it's clean. I used up one. It feels a bit slippery. I wonder if I should add a rinse. It is definitely too small to wash large cooking utensils like frying pans and pots together with the dishes (for a family of two). They just wash their dishes by hand. Anyway, although the drying function is disappointing, it is good to have a dishwasher. Don't suffer from plantar fasciitis and varicose veins later, and if you are hooked, buy it. -Additional review 2- If you are disappointed that there is no 'rinse only' function, you can use 'quick course' + 'add rinse' to finish washing the dishes cleanly in about 34 minutes (about 10 minutes of washing process - dehydration - 3 rinses = total 4 rinses). In fact, this is how I wash the dishes these days. Since I am a novice, I just invest 5 more minutes, put dishwashing detergent on a sponge, wipe it, and rinse it. It seems cleaner when I do it by hand, and I wonder if I bought it and made a fuss. I want to, but the dishwashing time and effort have been reduced incomparably compared to when there was no dishwasher. The condition of the dishes after washing is the best, boasting a shiny and glossy finish^^. (I don't use tablets, so I don't have to spend money on that) Electricity, water, and sewage bills, and hot water bills have also been reduced by tens of thousands of won compared to before the dishwasher (when I used a dish dryer), so I think this is enough. Thank you for reading the long review. Have a nice day^^

Comments (English): [ Price drop just two days after purchase? ] || ---------------- || If you bought it on Sunday and installed it on Tuesday morning and the price went down by 40,000 won in the meantime, would you feel good? Or not? It doesn't dry properly after washing the dishes. There's water on the cup that I turned over and there's moisture left on the silicone packing of the lunch box lid. Even though I left it wide open for 30-40 minutes, it was like that (there was still moisture left the next morning). You have to take the cup out and shake off the water. Don't be afraid of electricity and add the 'strong drying' stage to see about 80% drying effect and there are also fewer water stains. Standard course, basic 4 rinses (1:08) + strong drying = 1 hour 26 minutes, and if you add a rinse when there are a lot of dishes, it takes about 1 hour 37 minutes in total. (Since I run it after washing the dishes first, the standard course and basic rinse are enough). At first, I ran it on the strong drying cycle for a while, but since people are creatures of adaptation, I just roughly ran the standard cycle and after washing the dishes, I took out the Lock & Lock lid and cup, shook off the water, and put them back to dry. I had this problem when I used a large built-in before, so I considered using a dishwasher, but the dish dryer broke down, so I ended up getting a dishwasher. It seems that a dryer is the best for fluffy drying + sterilization! The dishwashing time was saved by half compared to usual, but it seems like a different type of annoying aftercare. I felt uncomfortable about having to leave the door open for drying, as I was worried that dust or flies might get in. I have no complaints about the installer. He was neat, kind, and installed it quickly. This is an honest review from a consumer who spent 40,000 won in two days and was very upset. -Additional review 1- As a detergent tip, even if it says 6 tablets, I don't think you need to put in every single tablet. I cut it into 5:5 parts with scissors and put it in a container and use it, and it's clean. I used up one. It feels a bit slippery. I wonder if I should add a rinse. It is definitely too small to wash large cooking utensils like frying pans and pots together with the dishes (for a family of two). They just wash their dishes by hand. Anyway, although the drying function is disappointing, it is good to have a dishwasher. Don't suffer from plantar fasciitis and varicose veins later, and if you are hooked, buy it. -Additional review 2- If you are disappointed that there is no 'rinse only' function, you can use 'quick course' + 'add rinse' to finish washing the dishes cleanly in about 34 minutes (about 10 minutes of washing process - dehydration - 3 rinses = total 4 rinses). In fact, this is how I wash the dishes these days. Since I am a novice, I just invest 5 more minutes, put dishwashing detergent on a sponge, wipe it, and rinse it. It seems cleaner when I do it by hand, and I wonder if I bought it and made a fuss. I want to, but the dishwashing time and effort have been reduced incomparably compared to when there was no dishwasher. The condition of the dishes after washing is the best, boasting a shiny and glossy finish^^. (I don't use tablets, so I don't have to spend money on that) Electricity, water, and sewage bills, and hot water bills have also been reduced by tens of thousands of won compared to before the dishwasher (when I used a dish dryer), so I think this is enough. Thank you for reading the long review. Have a nice day^^

Sentence (English): In fact, this is how I wash the dishes these days.
Comments (English): [ Price drop just two days after purchase? ] || ---------------- || If you bought it on Sunday and installed it on Tuesday morning and the price went down by 40,000 won in the meantime, would you feel good? Or not? It doesn't dry properly after washing the dishes. There's water on the cup that I turned over and there's moisture left on the silicone packing of the lunch box lid. Even though I left it wide open for 30-40 minutes, it was like that (there was still moisture left the next morning). You have to take the cup out and shake off the water. Don't be afraid of electricity and add the 'strong drying' stage to see about 80% drying effect and there are also fewer water stains. Standard course, basic 4 rinses (1:08) + strong drying = 1 hour 26 minutes, and if you add a rinse when there are a lot of dishes, it takes about 1 hour 37 minutes in total. (Since I run it after washing the dishes first, the standard course and basic rinse are enough). At first, I ran it on the strong drying cycle for a while, but since people are creatures of adaptation, I just roughly ran the standard cycle and after washing the dishes, I took out the Lock & Lock lid and cup, shook off the water, and put them back to dry. I had this problem when I used a large built-in before, so I considered using a dishwasher, but the dish dryer broke down, so I ended up getting a dishwasher. It seems that a dryer is the best for fluffy drying + sterilization! The dishwashing time was saved by half compared to usual, but it seems like a different type of annoying aftercare. I felt uncomfortable about having to leave the door open for drying, as I was worried that dust or flies might get in. I have no complaints about the installer. He was neat, kind, and installed it quickly. This is an honest review from a consumer who spent 40,000 won in two days and was very upset. -Additional review 1- As a detergent tip, even if it says 6 tablets, I don't think you need to put in every single tablet. I cut it into 5:5 parts with scissors and put it in a container and use it, and it's clean. I used up one. It feels a bit slippery. I wonder if I should add a rinse. It is definitely too small to wash large cooking utensils like frying pans and pots together with the dishes (for a family of two). They just wash their dishes by hand. Anyway, although the drying function is disappointing, it is good to have a dishwasher. Don't suffer from plantar fasciitis and varicose veins later, and if you are hooked, buy it. -Additional review 2- If you are disappointed that there is no 'rinse only' function, you can use 'quick course' + 'add rinse' to finish washing the dishes cleanly in about 34 minutes (about 10 minutes of washing process - dehydration - 3 rinses = total 4 rinses). In fact, this is how I wash the dishes these days. Since I am a novice, I just invest 5 more minutes, put dishwashing detergent on a sponge, wipe it, and rinse it. It seems cleaner when I do it by hand, and I wonder if I bought it and made a fuss. I want to, but the dishwashing time and effort have been reduced incomparably compared to when there was no dishwasher. The condition of the dishes after washing is the best, boasting a shiny and glossy finish^^. (I don't use tablets, so I don't have to spend money on that) Electricity, water, and sewage bills, and hot water bills have also been reduced by tens of thousands of won compared to before the dishwasher (when I used a dish dryer), so I think this is enough. Thank you for reading the long review. Have a nice day^^

Sentence (English): It seems cleaner when I do it by hand, and I wonder if I bought it and made a fuss.
Comments (English): [ Price drop just two days after purchase? ] || ---------------- || If you bought it on Sunday and installed it on Tuesday morning and the price went down by 40,000 won in the meantime, would you feel good? Or not? It doesn't dry properly after washing the dishes. There's water on the cup that I turned over and there's moisture left on the silicone packing of the lunch box lid. Even though I left it wide open for 30-40 minutes, it was like that (there was still moisture left the next morning). You have to take the cup out and shake off the water. Don't be afraid of electricity and add the 'strong drying' stage to see about 80% drying effect and there are also fewer water stains. Standard course, basic 4 rinses (1:08) + strong drying = 1 hour 26 minutes, and if you add a rinse when there are a lot of dishes, it takes about 1 hour 37 minutes in total. (Since I run it after washing the dishes first, the standard course and basic rinse are enough). At first, I ran it on the strong drying cycle for a while, but since people are creatures of adaptation, I just roughly ran the standard cycle and after washing the dishes, I took out the Lock & Lock lid and cup, shook off the water, and put them back to dry. I had this problem when I used a large built-in before, so I considered using a dishwasher, but the dish dryer broke down, so I ended up getting a dishwasher. It seems that a dryer is the best for fluffy drying + sterilization! The dishwashing time was saved by half compared to usual, but it seems like a different type of annoying aftercare. I felt uncomfortable about having to leave the door open for drying, as I was worried that dust or flies might get in. I have no complaints about the installer. He was neat, kind, and installed it quickly. This is an honest review from a consumer who spent 40,000 won in two days and was very upset. -Additional review 1- As a detergent tip, even if it says 6 tablets, I don't think you need to put in every single tablet. I cut it into 5:5 parts with scissors and put it in a container and use it, and it's clean. I used up one. It feels a bit slippery. I wonder if I should add a rinse. It is definitely too small to wash large cooking utensils like frying pans and pots together with the dishes (for a family of two). They just wash their dishes by hand. Anyway, although the drying function is disappointing, it is good to have a dishwasher. Don't suffer from plantar fasciitis and varicose veins later, and if you are hooked, buy it. -Additional review 2- If you are disappointed that there is no 'rinse only' function, you can use 'quick course' + 'add rinse' to finish washing the dishes cleanly in about 34 minutes (about 10 minutes of washing process - dehydration - 3 rinses = total 4 rinses). In fact, this is how I wash the dishes these days. Since I am a novice, I just invest 5 more minutes, put dishwashing detergent on a sponge, wipe it, and rinse it. It seems cleaner when I do it by hand, and I wonder if I bought it and made a fuss. I want to, but the dishwashing time and effort have been reduced incomparably compared to when there was no dishwasher. The condition of the dishes after washing is the best, boasting a shiny and glossy finish^^. (I don't use tablets, so I don't have to spend money on that) Electricity, water, and sewage bills, and hot water bills have also been reduced by tens of thousands of won compared to before the dishwasher (when I used a dish dryer), so I think this is enough. Thank you for reading the long review. Have a nice day^^

Sentence (English): I want to, but the dishwashing time and effort have been reduced incomparably compared to when there was no dishwasher.
Comments (English): [ Price drop just two days after purchase? ] || ---------------- || If you bought it on Sunday and installed it on Tuesday morning and the price went down by 40,000 won in the meantime, would you feel good? Or not? It doesn't dry properly after washing the dishes. There's water on the cup that I turned over and there's moisture left on the silicone packing of the lunch box lid. Even though I left it wide open for 30-40 minutes, it was like that (there was still moisture left the next morning). You have to take the cup out and shake off the water. Don't be afraid of electricity and add the 'strong drying' stage to see about 80% drying effect and there are also fewer water stains. Standard course, basic 4 rinses (1:08) + strong drying = 1 hour 26 minutes, and if you add a rinse when there are a lot of dishes, it takes about 1 hour 37 minutes in total. (Since I run it after washing the dishes first, the standard course and basic rinse are enough). At first, I ran it on the strong drying cycle for a while, but since people are creatures of adaptation, I just roughly ran the standard cycle and after washing the dishes, I took out the Lock & Lock lid and cup, shook off the water, and put them back to dry. I had this problem when I used a large built-in before, so I considered using a dishwasher, but the dish dryer broke down, so I ended up getting a dishwasher. It seems that a dryer is the best for fluffy drying + sterilization! The dishwashing time was saved by half compared to usual, but it seems like a different type of annoying aftercare. I felt uncomfortable about having to leave the door open for drying, as I was worried that dust or flies might get in. I have no complaints about the installer. He was neat, kind, and installed it quickly. This is an honest review from a consumer who spent 40,000 won in two days and was very upset. -Additional review 1- As a detergent tip, even if it says 6 tablets, I don't think you need to put in every single tablet. I cut it into 5:5 parts with scissors and put it in a container and use it, and it's clean. I used up one. It feels a bit slippery. I wonder if I should add a rinse. It is definitely too small to wash large cooking utensils like frying pans and pots together with the dishes (for a family of two). They just wash their dishes by hand. Anyway, although the drying function is disappointing, it is good to have a dishwasher. Don't suffer from plantar fasciitis and varicose veins later, and if you are hooked, buy it. -Additional review 2- If you are disappointed that there is no 'rinse only' function, you can use 'quick course' + 'add rinse' to finish washing the dishes cleanly in about 34 minutes (about 10 minutes of washing process - dehydration - 3 rinses = total 4 rinses). In fact, this is how I wash the dishes these days. Since I am a novice, I just invest 5 more minutes, put dishwashing detergent on a sponge, wipe it, and rinse it. It seems cleaner when I do it by hand, and I wonder if I bought it and made a fuss. I want to, but the dishwashing time and effort have been reduced incomparably compared to when there was no dishwasher. The condition of the dishes after washing is the best, boasting a shiny and glossy finish^^. (I don't use tablets, so I don't have to spend money on that) Electricity, water, and sewage bills, and hot water bills have also been reduced by tens of thousands of won compared to before the dishwasher (when I used a dish dryer), so I think this is enough. Thank you for reading the long review. Have a nice day^^

Sentence (English): The condition of the dishes after washing is the best, boasting a shiny and glossy finish^^. (I don't use tablets, so I don't have to spend money on that) Electricity, water, and sewage bills, and hot water bills have also been reduced by tens of thousands of won compared to before the dishwasher (when I used a dish dryer), so I think this is enough.
Comments (English): [ Price drop just two days after purchase? ] || ---------------- || If you bought it on Sunday and installed it on Tuesday morning and the price went down by 40,000 won in the meantime, would you feel good? Or not? It doesn't dry properly after washing the dishes. There's water on the cup that I turned over and there's moisture left on the silicone packing of the lunch box lid. Even though I left it wide open for 30-40 minutes, it was like that (there was still moisture left the next morning). You have to take the cup out and shake off the water. Don't be afraid of electricity and add the 'strong drying' stage to see about 80% drying effect and there are also fewer water stains. Standard course, basic 4 rinses (1:08) + strong drying = 1 hour 26 minutes, and if you add a rinse when there are a lot of dishes, it takes about 1 hour 37 minutes in total. (Since I run it after washing the dishes first, the standard course and basic rinse are enough). At first, I ran it on the strong drying cycle for a while, but since people are creatures of adaptation, I just roughly ran the standard cycle and after washing the dishes, I took out the Lock & Lock lid and cup, shook off the water, and put them back to dry. I had this problem when I used a large built-in before, so I considered using a dishwasher, but the dish dryer broke down, so I ended up getting a dishwasher. It seems that a dryer is the best for fluffy drying + sterilization! The dishwashing time was saved by half compared to usual, but it seems like a different type of annoying aftercare. I felt uncomfortable about having to leave the door open for drying, as I was worried that dust or flies might get in. I have no complaints about the installer. He was neat, kind, and installed it quickly. This is an honest review from a consumer who spent 40,000 won in two days and was very upset. -Additional review 1- As a detergent tip, even if it says 6 tablets, I don't think you need to put in every single tablet. I cut it into 5:5 parts with scissors and put it in a container and use it, and it's clean. I used up one. It feels a bit slippery. I wonder if I should add a rinse. It is definitely too small to wash large cooking utensils like frying pans and pots together with the dishes (for a family of two). They just wash their dishes by hand. Anyway, although the drying function is disappointing, it is good to have a dishwasher. Don't suffer from plantar fasciitis and varicose veins later, and if you are hooked, buy it. -Additional review 2- If you are disappointed that there is no 'rinse only' function, you can use 'quick course' + 'add rinse' to finish washing the dishes cleanly in about 34 minutes (about 10 minutes of washing process - dehydration - 3 rinses = total 4 rinses). In fact, this is how I wash the dishes these days. Since I am a novice, I just invest 5 more minutes, put dishwashing detergent on a sponge, wipe it, and rinse it. It seems cleaner when I do it by hand, and I wonder if I bought it and made a fuss. I want to, but the dishwashing time and effort have been reduced incomparably compared to when there was no dishwasher. The condition of the dishes after washing is the best, boasting a shiny and glossy finish^^. (I don't use tablets, so I don't have to spend money on that) Electricity, water, and sewage bills, and hot water bills have also been reduced by tens of thousands of won compared to before the dishwasher (when I used a dish dryer), so I think this is enough. Thank you for reading the long review. Have a nice day^^

Comments (English): [ Price drop just two days after purchase? ] || ---------------- || If you bought it on Sunday and installed it on Tuesday morning and the price went down by 40,000 won in the meantime, would you feel good? Or not? It doesn't dry properly after washing the dishes. There's water on the cup that I turned over and there's moisture left on the silicone packing of the lunch box lid. Even though I left it wide open for 30-40 minutes, it was like that (there was still moisture left the next morning). You have to take the cup out and shake off the water. Don't be afraid of electricity and add the 'strong drying' stage to see about 80% drying effect and there are also fewer water stains. Standard course, basic 4 rinses (1:08) + strong drying = 1 hour 26 minutes, and if you add a rinse when there are a lot of dishes, it takes about 1 hour 37 minutes in total. (Since I run it after washing the dishes first, the standard course and basic rinse are enough). At first, I ran it on the strong drying cycle for a while, but since people are creatures of adaptation, I just roughly ran the standard cycle and after washing the dishes, I took out the Lock & Lock lid and cup, shook off the water, and put them back to dry. I had this problem when I used a large built-in before, so I considered using a dishwasher, but the dish dryer broke down, so I ended up getting a dishwasher. It seems that a dryer is the best for fluffy drying + sterilization! The dishwashing time was saved by half compared to usual, but it seems like a different type of annoying aftercare. I felt uncomfortable about having to leave the door open for drying, as I was worried that dust or flies might get in. I have no complaints about the installer. He was neat, kind, and installed it quickly. This is an honest review from a consumer who spent 40,000 won in two days and was very upset. -Additional review 1- As a detergent tip, even if it says 6 tablets, I don't think you need to put in every single tablet. I cut it into 5:5 parts with scissors and put it in a container and use it, and it's clean. I used up one. It feels a bit slippery. I wonder if I should add a rinse. It is definitely too small to wash large cooking utensils like frying pans and pots together with the dishes (for a family of two). They just wash their dishes by hand. Anyway, although the drying function is disappointing, it is good to have a dishwasher. Don't suffer from plantar fasciitis and varicose veins later, and if you are hooked, buy it. -Additional review 2- If you are disappointed that there is no 'rinse only' function, you can use 'quick course' + 'add rinse' to finish washing the dishes cleanly in about 34 minutes (about 10 minutes of washing process - dehydration - 3 rinses = total 4 rinses). In fact, this is how I wash the dishes these days. Since I am a novice, I just invest 5 more minutes, put dishwashing detergent on a sponge, wipe it, and rinse it. It seems cleaner when I do it by hand, and I wonder if I bought it and made a fuss. I want to, but the dishwashing time and effort have been reduced incomparably compared to when there was no dishwasher. The condition of the dishes after washing is the best, boasting a shiny and glossy finish^^. (I don't use tablets, so I don't have to spend money on that) Electricity, water, and sewage bills, and hot water bills have also been reduced by tens of thousands of won compared to before the dishwasher (when I used a dish dryer), so I think this is enough. Thank you for reading the long review. Have a nice day^^

Sentence (English): I'm a family of 4, but I don't want to disassemble the lower cabinet, so I searched for a week for 6-person ones~ The search results showed that the top 3 6-person dishwashers are S*Mae*, L*, and Samsung.
Comments (English): [ Satisfied with the cleaning power, dissatisfied with the installation ] || ---------------- || I'm a family of 4, but I don't want to disassemble the lower cabinet, so I searched for a week for 6-person ones~ The search results showed that the top 3 6-person dishwashers are S*Mae*, L*, and Samsung. After analyzing the pros and cons and measuring the size, I chose Samsung. Beige was cheaper than white and beige, but since all the appliances in my house are silver, I think I made a good purchase of beige. ((Installation review)) - I wanted the dishwasher door to face the sink, but because of the drying rack on the upper cabinet, I had no choice but to install it facing forward. I think you need to consider not only the height but also the door opening position when calculating. - Some of the comments said that the installers were unfriendly, but so did I. They kept complaining that they couldn't find it even after sending the wire down from the sink plate to the hole, so I had to lie down and look for it. There are many more, but I won't write any further. Anyway, the installation went well. ((Product review)) - I should've bought the dishwasher sooner. It's very good. I throw the frog detergent in half and use it on the floor, and it washes very cleanly. - It's perfect for a family of 4, running it twice a day, morning and evening. If it was for 12 people, I would have had to collect the dishes and do it, but I like that I can do it right after eating. - The standard course is an hour and a few minutes, so it's about an hour, so if you run it like a washing machine and forget about it, it's over. - The automatic door opening function is highly recommended. Even if you don't buy this product, it's better to buy one that has an automatic door opening function. ((Other)) - When I opened the filter, there was always about 1 cm of water at the bottom, so I thought it was broken, but when I checked, it was normal for water to always be filled to prevent sewage odor. - I've run it 7-8 times since I bought it, and I always remove and put food scraps in, so the filter is clean, but there's a slight fishy smell. They said that putting vinegar in a small bowl and running the sterilization course will work, so I'll have to try that.

Sentence (English): This dishwasher purchase was a mistake.
Comments (English): This dishwasher purchase was a mistake. The biggest issue is the lower rack, most dishes don't fit into the prongs, I am seriously considering getting a wire cutter and trying to cut some of them off to make it more usable. Right now I balance larger dishes on top of the prongs or just wash them by hand. Needless to say, not as many dishes fit. I do like the upper third rack, it is handy for utensils. Overall, the dishwasher does wash and mostly dry the dishes. The controls are not particularly intuitive, they could have done much better, but thank goodness for You Tube! Oh, and now I have a drip under my sink, its not much, just a tiny puddle when the dishwasher drains. I bought this product because it is supposed to sense for leaks, a problem my old dishwasher had developed. It seems I STILL have a leak, just in a different location where there is no sensor. It has been a frustration.

Comments (English): [ Poor construction and customer service by Bosch ] || ---------------- || I have owned 2 previous Bosch dishwashers which I loved, and then purchased this new Bosch 800 dishwasher in August 2024 from Costco. Right after I purchased it, I left on vacation and then was in the hospital, and I was not able to use it during the first 3 months following installation. Costco is great with customer service, I contacted them since I was having a problem, but since I had just gone over 90 days of having the dishwasher, they could not return it and told me I had to contact Bosch customer service.The issue is with my bottom rack, which has been redesigned from the previous rack and is terrible to use. When it has dishes on it, it tilts backward when it's pushed in. I've had broken dishes on several occasions unless I am extremely careful when pushing the rack in. Also, the utensil rack is very flimsy and difficult to fit utensils in when using the dividers. I think that these racks are very poorly designed and constructed for what should be a premium dishwasher.I contacted Bosch service and they had a technician come to my house. He indicated that he felt that I was using it correctly, and that I would have to contact Bosch for further help. I asked that they either take the dishwasher back and give me a refund, or provide me with a new bottom rack that is the same design as the original. After more than several attempts to get it rectified, they have indicated that they will not do either and I am now very disappointed by Bosch. I have recommended Bosch to many friends and family members after my previous experience but will not do so again. I expected much better construction, as well as superior customer service. I did not want to provide this rating, but after waiting so long and trying to work with them to get the problem rectified, I feel that I have no other option.
